title: Attempting to add GDScript to autoload fails with unclear error if class_name present in script
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7.1-stable

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04 - Godot 4.7.1-stable (not mono)

### Issue description

After creating a GDScript class with `class_name` at the top of the file, it's impossible to add that file to autoloads in the project settings. Instead, a confusing error appears that is not descriptive of the issue:

> Can't add Autoload:
> TweenLibrary is an invalid name. Must not collide with an existing global script class name.

Note: I don't think this is a duplicate. #120706 refers to the popup being blank, and #119055 was closed by #119086, which from the discussion appears only to introduce a prompt to add a name if the class name conflicts with a global class already in the list.
I believe this is slightly different: firstly a class with class_name already present can't be added to the list of globals at all (this may have been fixed by the pull request, I'm not sure), and secondly the error message is misleading - there is no class already in the list with the same name as the one being added. Apologies for the spam if I've misunderstoof the discussion in the PR though!

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new GDScript class
2. Add `class_name` to the beginning with a relevant class name
3. Open Project Settings>Globals>Autoload
4. Click Select Script/Scene and select the new script
5. Observe error message

In attached MRP, script file is `Example.gd` and class_name is `Example`, and the list of globals is empty.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[autoload-classname-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30365716/autoload-classname-mrp.zip)
